title: Grateful Dead Live at Civic Auditorium on 1970-03-07

ai_review.summary: A good‑quality audience tape that delivers a high‑energy 1970 performance highlighted by a scorching China > Rider > High Time, epic Lovelight and blistering Not Fade Away.
ai_review.review: Despite the inherent limitations of an early‑70s AUD, the recording is listenable enough to showcase one of the band’s most intense shows – tight transitions, ferocious jams and standout moments like Black Peter, China > Rider > High Time and a marathon Lovelight. Reviewers rave about Jerry’s searing guitar, Phil’s bass drive and the unstoppable drummers, while noting the tape’s occasional hiss, pops and pitch quirks.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the musical performance (many 4‑5 star comments) while acknowledging consistent but tolerable audio flaws; weighted average yields a solid four‑star rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Audible hiss, occasional pops, splices and pitch issues are noted, but the tape remains listenable with clear instrument separation; no soundboard source available.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows with high‑octane transitions – a fiery China > Rider > High Time, followed by an extended NFA/Drums/Good Lovin'/The Other One/Lovelight sequence that keeps the energy relentless.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers highlight his scorching guitar tone, fast‑paced solos and emotive vocals on Black Peter and High Time.
band_member_comments.Phil: Praised for a ‘machine‑gun’ bass intro into Good Lovin' and overall driving low end throughout the jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted for burning rhythm/lead work during China > Rider and contributing to the high‑energy feel.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s vocal power is repeatedly mentioned; organ solos are sparse but his presence is felt.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey and Bill receive enthusiastic praise for a tribal, powerful drum segment that propels the NFA/Drums sequence.
